fix: And I heard it even more precisely from Masannasus [...], who
reason: Greek marks a gap after Μασαννάσου; sense survives but the gap must be marked, not smoothed.
Μικίψης has iota, not upsilon; Micipsa is the standard form and this is the only occurrence in the corpus.

fix: ten ships sailing in company with him
reason: ὁμοπλοούσας means sailing together, in company; nothing about speed.

fix: made their way, against all expectation, back to Aspis
reason: παραδόξως means unexpectedly, not with difficulty; keep 'back' as in the original wording.
Not an error: 'plausibility' and 'spectators' make the referent clear (tragedy); the English matches the Greek's ἐκείνοις/τούτοις.

fix: they were utterly ruined and lost their homeland because of their loyalty to the Achaeans
reason: ἔπταισαν τῇ πατρίδι: came to grief in respect of their city, i.e. lost it; 'for' wrongly suggests on its behalf.

fix: Time and again the Romans paid no attention to them, but at this point they dispatched envoys
reason: παρακούω here does mean disregard; the error is πλεονάκις, which means repeatedly, not 'for a long while'.

fix: in the territory of whichever is being attacked
reason: τῶν πολεμουμένων is passive: the party being warred upon.

fix: he had in effect handed over the whole of his command to the latter
reason: Singular τούτῳ after 'Dorimachus and Scopas': likely Scopas (the nearest name, who then acts), but ambiguous; English silently chose Dorimachus.

fix: They treated all the others in the same way
reason: τοῖς ἄλλοις πᾶσι means all the others; 'of that party' is added and narrows the sense.
